project.name: LumiNails
project.productType: beauty salon service and booking website

design.colorMode: light public UI; light and dark admin UI

typography.character: sans headings and functional body; existing serif identity detail

spacing.base: 4px (observed spacing rhythm, not a separate runtime scale)
spacing.adminWorkspace: 28px top / 42px inline / 50px bottom; responsive local variants

radius.hero: full-width desktop photo; uncropped 16:9 mobile image with copy left, benefits at bottom, gallery row and separate actions below; section boundaries have no outer radius

shadows.exceptions: Existing booking path, account tab, compact admin control, focus and overlay shadows are retained locally; detailed vocabulary is in .impeccable/design.json.

motion.rule: Use implemented component-specific transitions and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

design.density: open public sections; compact admin workspace with grouped metrics
design.authority: Implemented TEST source and review captures; no approved new comp
design.directionName: Minimal studio (descriptive working name, not an additional brand commitment)

patterns: full-width photographic hero with DM Sans title and factual location below it
four image-top service cards; two at 900px, one at 768px
flat three-image desktop gallery rail with retained arrows, swipe and keyboard logic
two-column gallery page with consistent caption overlays; one column at 640px
contained service text and untinted 3:2 contain image
retained progressive booking and account/guest paths
white admin navigation, one grouped metric container and divided task panels
navy admin dark theme and mobile drawer at 900px

must: Edit source CSS and rebuild generated bundles
Keep public and admin CSS ownership separate
Use semantic tokens and visible focus states
Keep public mobile fields at least 16px, visible focus and existing touch areas; retain compact admin geometry and its 44px expanded button hit areas
Read docs/design-system.md and docs/visual-audit.md before UI changes
Use root DESIGN.md for detailed extracted tokens and docs/design-system.md for ownership and bounded checks
avoid: Do not edit style.css or admin-v2.css directly
Do not use !important or duplicate override layers
Do not enable zoom in standalone admin PWA
Do not run tests in GitHub Actions
Do not use decorative glass or gradients without a functional reason
Do not treat preserved local radius exceptions as new global tiers

decisions.decision: Replace the prior visual direction with cobalt actions, white/cool-gray surfaces and DM Sans content headings across public and admin UI. Use a full-width desktop hero, contained introduction, four image-top service cards, a flat gallery rail, a compact white footer, and grouped admin metrics with white navigation and a navy dark theme.
decisions.reason: The user requested a genuinely different minimalist layout and colors for both surfaces, a large full-width hero, and allowed copy changes. The implementation keeps real photos, prices, data sources and workflows, plus the existing mobile 16:9 contain framing and admin PWA zoom policy. This is code-led implemented evidence, not a new approved comp.

decisions.decision: Use limestone, ivory, mist teal and deep ink consistently across public and admin light/dark UI, and make the desktop homepage hero a full-width photographic canvas.
decisions.reason: The user requested a new minimal palette and full-page hero. Existing CMS imagery and site typography stay intact; semantic tokens and directional scrims preserve legibility and mobile 16:9 composition.

decisions.decision: Compress the homepage gallery transitions and shared footer, remove the redundant inner gallery title, and present service-detail heroes as an untinted 3:2 image plus neutral copy on mobile.
decisions.reason: The previous transition, footer and service heroes consumed disproportionate screen space. The new treatment keeps 44px targets, full imagery and readable hierarchy without adding a component dependency; a 21st.dev search only informed the understated arrow CTA styling.

decisions.decision: Keep the homepage notice, gallery transition and shared footer compact; center the mobile hero benefits and use a balanced two-column action row. Preserve public page zoom while keeping form controls large enough to prevent iOS focus zoom.
decisions.reason: The previous vertical rhythm consumed too much of a phone screen, while narrow footer columns harmed readability. Compact spacing must come from layout and redundant copy, not from shrinking touch targets or form text.

decisions.decision: Replace the public pink primary and pink-tinted surfaces with pearl sage and neutral ivory, simplify the mobile hero into one image composition, and remove the homepage carousel glow and card shadows.
decisions.reason: The user rejected the visible pink and the fragmented hero, while the clipped carousel shadow created an obvious edge artifact. Slate-on-sage and slate-on-ivory keep strong contrast without changing public flows or the admin theme.

decisions.decision: Keep the mobile hero image exactly 16:9 without cropping or zoom, place all three benefit labels on the photo, and replace the broad overlay with text-local translucent backgrounds.
decisions.reason: The user plans to upload 16:9 images and needs predictable framing. Compact mobile typography fits the fixed image height; desktop layout remains unchanged.

decisions.decision: Use an edge-to-edge mobile hero photo with left-aligned slate text over a light readability scrim and account actions below the image.
decisions.reason: The user requested a desktop-inspired mobile hero and removal of brown hero text. Preserve the CMS image and copy, desktop split layout, and existing action links.

decisions.decision: Adopt a quiet-luxury editorial redesign for the TEST critical views.
decisions.reason: The user explicitly approved a redesign; the direction preserves LumiNails imagery and typography while improving hierarchy, booking clarity, contrast and responsive behavior.

decisions.decision: Use deep cacao as the primary action and dark showcase color, with warm ivory surfaces and muted blush accents.
decisions.reason: This keeps the beauty-studio character while providing stronger text and control contrast than the previous dusty rose primary.

decisions.decision: Treat the mobile hero image and gallery label as one framed card, and suppress the account recommendation when the hero already includes an account action.
decisions.reason: A single radius owner prevents broken nested corners, while removing the adjacent duplicate account promotion restores a clear homepage action hierarchy.

decisions.decision: Restore the original quiet-luxury public and admin color systems while retaining the later layout and responsive fixes.
decisions.reason: The five-color earth-tone experiment flattened the interface hierarchy; the approved original semantic tokens provide clearer surfaces, states and readable contrast.

decisions.decision: Use one shared 1200px content width and responsive section padding, while keeping the desktop home hero full-bleed.
decisions.reason: Introduction, services and gallery align to the same gutters; the hero no longer clips its visual, and account and booking utility layouts retain desktop proportions.

decisions.decision: Implement the supplied Figma system with Playfair Display, DM Sans, a slate/pink/greige palette, sharp component radii, consistent gallery captions, and one shared public footer.
decisions.reason: The user supplied an editable Figma source and explicitly requested implementation across desktop, mobile, public pages, and admin while preserving the current homepage gallery imagery.

decisions.decision: Use #FFD1DC as the shared public and admin primary pink.
decisions.reason: The user explicitly selected the lighter pink for every component using the primary brand color.
